rule: GOAL: Clear the level by depleting the step budget bar. CONTROLS: Clicking cells only reduces the timer; it does not move objects. RULE: The pink bar shrinks with every action, acting as a hard limit. TRAP: Clicking specific objects like gates or arrows for effects wastes time.

GOAL: Align the floating platform so paint streams from its edges into the yellow notches below. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the platform horizontally; Space releases the paint pour. RULE: Paint spills exactly four columns beyond each end of the platform, so position the platform to guide these outer streams into the targets. TRAP: Thinking the paint pours straight down from the center; it actually flows off the sides, requiring careful horizontal alignment.

GOAL: Jump over gray pegs to land on white squares, reaching the green target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move two spaces orthogonally, leaping over an intervening peg. RULE: You only land on squares of the same parity, using gray pegs as bridges between white nodes. TRAP: Believing you can step one space onto a gray peg; you must always jump two spaces to a white square.

GOAL: Extend the green bar's tip to touch the red plus marker. CONTROLS: Click the right panel of the box to lengthen the bar; click the left panel to shorten it. RULE: The bar only moves when you click the box's side panels, not the bar itself or the plus. TRAP: Assuming the red dot marks a target location; it simply moves with the bar's tip as a handle.

GOAL: Guide the ball to the exit by manipulating five keys. CONTROLS: Click keys to toggle bar and stem colors; click ball to run. RULE: Dark bars activate keys; stem color sets direction, with light sending left and dark sending down. TRAP: Assuming all keys move the ball wastes time; only those with dark bars trigger action.

GOAL: Move the glowing square to the center of the gray orb. CONTROLS: Clicking a distant dot teleports the square to that spot, swapping places. RULE: You can only jump to a dot if there are no more than two intermediate dots between you and the target. TRAP: Thinking you must step through every dot; skipping ahead is allowed and often necessary to reach the core.

GOAL: Slide the plunger knob to the left handle using three precise moves. CONTROLS: Use left arrow keys to shift the knob two columns inward per press. RULE: Each press moves the knob exactly two columns, requiring three presses to reach the target. TRAP: Believing the knob stops at the shaft’s start; it actually locks only at the handle.

GOAL: Clear the level by moving the green block through the wall gap using exactly four clicks. CONTROLS: Top pad expands white volume; right pad moves the player; left and bottom pads adjust position or shrink volume. RULE: The player’s movement range is strictly limited by the current boundary of the white region. TRAP: Assuming the player could move freely to the gap regardless of the white region’s size wasted time.

GOAL: Move the large knob through a narrow, teeth-lined channel to reach the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the knob; clicking white pattern tiles shrinks its size. RULE: The knob must match the passage width; shrink it by completing the pattern to pass. TRAP: Assuming the knob fits everywhere; forcing a large knob into a narrow gap wastes moves.

GOAL: Guide the knob to the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob. RULE: The knob fits the channel only when aligned with its width. TRAP: Assuming the knob could move down anywhere in the open area, rather than strictly within the narrow channel.

GOAL: Match the pink glyph under each blue letter to its designated partner. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between slots; pressing UP rotates the wheel to change the glyph. RULE: Each blue letter has a fixed pink partner; the wheel is a cycle, so you can always reach the target by rotating. TRAP: Assuming the wheel order is random or fixed per slot; it is a consistent cycle, allowing you to predict the shortest rotation direction.

GOAL: Align the ring and body to slide into the frame. CONTROLS: Arrows move the linked pair; Space absorbs a nearby block. RULE: The ring must trail the body to clear the frame’s entrance. TRAP: Thinking the ring leads; it must follow, or the body jams against the wall.

GOAL: Reach the exit without triggering the guard’s lethal patrol. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the player until hitting a wall or obstacle. RULE: The guard instantly captures you if you share its row or column. TRAP: Assuming the guard stays still; it actively hunts you along its line of sight.

GOAL: Rotate yellow symbols to match the target sequence derived from the pink row. CONTROLS: Arrow keys spin the selected wheel slot to change its displayed symbol. RULE: Each pink symbol maps to a specific yellow target based on the legend’s row and column coordinates. TRAP: Assuming legend coordinates were column then row; they are actually row then column, causing wrong symbol lookups.

ESTABLISHED: The cursor is trapped in the upper rows. The bottom-right block is immovable and blocks access to the lower slots. The current arrangement violates the expected horizontal alignment. FAILED: Attempts to reach the bottom row or move the trapped block have been rejected by the game rules. Pushing blocks into occupied slots does nothing. GOAL IS NOT: A vertical stack order of Red, Navy, and Blue in the left column. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor. Actions push adjacent blocks. Moves into occupied or out-of-bounds spaces are ignored.

GOAL: Float three colored blocks to match the row of their corresponding wall gaps. CONTROLS: Click columns to raise fluid levels and lift floating players. RULE: A block aligns when its row matches the gap row, regardless of horizontal distance. TRAP: Assuming blocks must physically touch the wall to trigger alignment wastes clicks; only vertical row matching matters.

GOAL: Fill the safe's empty slots to match the color sequence shown at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a colored block in the bottom tray to select it, then click an empty slot in the middle safe to place that color. RULE: Each color must go into the specific slot that aligns vertically with its target color in the top row. TRAP: Thinking you can place colors in any order; the top row dictates the exact left-to-right sequence required for the safe to open.

GOAL: Align seven yellow letter wheels to match the target sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP and DOWN rotate the selected wheel. RULE: All wheels share one fixed cyclic order, allowing you to calculate exact rotation counts for each slot. TRAP: Assuming wheels rotate independently or have different orders; recognizing the shared cycle enables minimal, precise moves instead of blind trial.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to eliminate both guards while surviving their attacks. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per press. RULE: Guards only attack within the specific direction they are facing. TRAP: Assuming guards attack along their entire row or column regardless of facing direction.

GOAL: Transform the starting bar into the target bar by cycling glyphs through a hidden intermediate color. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the current glyph through its color’s sequence, skipping invalid decoys. RULE: Each glyph follows a strict two-step chain: Source to Intermediate, then Intermediate to Target. TRAP: Assuming all visible symbols are valid; some are decoys that break the chain and must be cycled past.

GOAL: Place each cross center at the intersection of its matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected cross three spaces; spacebar switches which cross is active. RULE: The center must share a row with two dots and a column with the other two. TRAP: Assuming you can move one space; steps are always three, so align coordinates by threes.

GOAL: Sort colors into boxes by following the pipe flow, ensuring downstream slots match their source. CONTROLS: Click a palette color to select it, then click a grid slot to place it; press space to submit. RULE: Colors flow through the pipe, so fill the connected box before the independent one to maintain sequence integrity. TRAP: Assuming boxes fill independently; ignoring the pipe’s directional dependency causes mismatches and wasted moves.

GOAL: Arrange seven letters into three colored boxes using specific pipe connections. CONTROLS: Click a letter from the bottom palette, then click its target slot inside the boxes. Press space to test the arrangement. RULE: Fill red slots first, then green, then blue, skipping the empty pipe mouths entirely. TRAP: Believing pipe mouths hold letters. They are just visual connectors; trying to place a letter there wastes time.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to align the yellow block with the target bracket. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to shift the ring one step counter-clockwise. RULE: The ring rotates as a whole unit; blocks do not move independently. TRAP: Clicking the green arrow or empty space wastes moves and drains the timer.

GOAL: Guide the blob to the ring by manipulating the cursor and bead positions. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move cursor; click the gray bead to swap it with the cursor. RULE: The blob always moves to the midpoint between the cursor and the gray bead. TRAP: Thinking the blob moves directly toward the click target; it only shifts relative to the bead's new location.

GOAL: Sequence seven colored blocks to match a target string. CONTROLS: Click pieces to select, click slots to place, press Space to scan. RULE: Placing the ring in a red slot bridges red and green groups, fixing the scan order. TRAP: Assuming the ring counts as a sequence position; it only marks the connection point, not a value.

GOAL: Align three geometric shapes—X, plus, and diamond—so their centers match specific target dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the active shape three pixels per press; Space switches focus to the next shape. RULE: Each shape has unique coverage: X hits diagonals, plus hits cross lines, diamond hits fixed distances. TRAP: Assuming Space rotates shapes; it only changes which shape you are currently moving.

GOAL: Clear the board by jumping pegs over neighbors into empty spaces. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click the empty landing spot to move. RULE: Jumps must go straight over exactly one adjacent peg into the space immediately beyond it. TRAP: Clicking the landing spot alone does nothing; you must first click the peg you want to move.

GOAL: Place each block inside its matching ring outline. CONTROLS: Click a block to select it, then use arrow keys to move it three steps at a time. RULE: Blocks can pass through ring lines, so position them so they completely cover the lighter interior area. TRAP: Assuming ring borders block movement wastes time; they are visual guides only, not solid walls.

GOAL: Move shapes to cover all eight dots without overlap errors. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the selected piece; space switches which piece is active. RULE: Only pixels exactly on a shape’s line count, not its filled interior. TRAP: Assuming dots inside the diamond’s center were covered by its boundary.

GOAL: Match the active panel’s outer grid to the color pattern shown in its central ring. CONTROLS: Click outer grid cells to toggle their colors between blue and red. RULE: White ring segments indicate red outer cells; gray segments indicate blue outer cells. TRAP: Assuming the ring rotates or the center cell changes the rule, rather than acting as a static key.

GOAL: Align your current shape with the target shape shown at the top to unlock the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character block across the grid floor. RULE: The legend at the bottom displays your active piece; it must match the static target image exactly. TRAP: Assuming walls were just obstacles; they actually block rotation paths, forcing you to navigate around them to change your piece's orientation.

GOAL: Paint grid cells to match the color patterns dictated by the two dials. CONTROLS: Click dial centers to rotate their rings; click empty cells to toggle their colors. RULE: Dial ring segments map to neighbor cells: white marks require red, gray marks require blue. TRAP: Assuming dials act independently; they overlap, so shared cells must satisfy both keys simultaneously.

GOAL: Place rings to split colored tokens into two matching, mirrored groups. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, click board slots to place, and press Space to submit. RULE: The two blue groups must be identical in sequence or exact reversals of each other. TRAP: Assuming adjacent rings are required; spacing them correctly is essential for the mirror pattern.

GOAL: Match ring colors to cell colors by rotating four dials. CONTROLS: Click dials to rotate rings clockwise. RULE: Dial center color dictates mapping: orange centers make white rings orange, red centers make white rings red. TRAP: Assuming all dials use the same color mapping ignores center color differences.

GOAL: Place rings and solids to fill empty slots in four boxes so their contents match the target sequence. CONTROLS: Click a palette item to select it, click a slot to place it, and press space to submit. RULE: Each box's filled slots, read left to right, must exactly match the corresponding segment of the target color string. TRAP: Assuming box positions determine the target order, when only the slot sequence matters regardless of screen location.

GOAL: Move both yellow markers into the target brackets on the bottom row. CONTROLS: Left button cycles the top loop; right button shifts the bottom row sideways. RULE: The top loop feeds items into the bottom row, so position them before shifting. TRAP: Trying to move both markers simultaneously causes collisions; park one safely first.

GOAL: Move two separate balls into the exact same grid cell. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both balls simultaneously in that direction. RULE: Yellow walls block movement, but balls can occupy the same space. TRAP: Assuming balls block each other; they actually pass through and stack.

GOAL: Move the plus to a spot where its arms cover the target fill area. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plus; Space activates the probe. RULE: Any overlap between an arm and the fill cells registers a match. TRAP: Believing you need deep overlap; a single touching cell is sufficient to clear the level.

ESTABLISHED: The ghost records only effective moves, ignoring blocked attempts. FAILED: Moving the ghost to the switch failed to open the door; it likely requires the player's presence. GOAL IS NOT: A remote trigger mechanism for the door. CONTROLS: Space records the current path for the ghost; standard keys move the player.

GOAL: Place two colored tiles onto their matching brackets. CONTROLS: Red buttons move tiles forward; green buttons move them backward. RULE: Tiles must land exactly on the bracket of their own color to win. TRAP: Assuming green moves tiles forward like red wastes turns; it actually reverses direction.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit box within the move limit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; specific keys rotate the character. RULE: The character must match the exit box’s exact orientation to finish the level. TRAP: Moving into a wall is a wasted move, not a blocked action that preserves your turn.

GOAL: Lure a ghost onto a switch to open a door, then escape. CONTROLS: Arrows move you; ghosts move on a fixed loop per turn. RULE: Ghosts follow your recorded path exactly, one step behind. TRAP: Thinking you must avoid the ghost; overlapping is safe, only the switch matters.

GOAL: Rotate the yellow and orange tokens along two intersecting loops to reach the target spots. CONTROLS: Click the top, bottom, left, or right edges to spin the corresponding vertical or horizontal ring. RULE: Each ring is one continuous loop of twenty cells; the ends wrap around to the other side, not a separate segment. TRAP: Assuming the top and bottom halves of a column are independent cycles causes misplaced moves at the wrap-around points.

GOAL: Use recorded ghosts to hold switches simultaneously. CONTROLS: Arrows move, Space records and replays actions. RULE: A ghost stays on a switch to keep its door open. TRAP: Moving a ghost after it clamps breaks the hold and closes the door.

GOAL: Set three dials to paint white cells with their center color and gray cells with red. CONTROLS: Click a dial to cycle its center color; click empty space to confirm. RULE: White cells take the dial’s center color, while gray cells always become red. TRAP: Assuming gray cells also take the dial’s center color leads to incorrect patterns and wasted time.

GOAL: Fill the four rings with their matching blocks. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected block; clicks select a block by its dot. RULE: A block fits a ring only if its dimensions exactly match the ring's interior. TRAP: Assuming any block could fit any ring; ignoring exact size mismatches wasted moves.

GOAL: Relocate a gray bead to a specific target to complete the puzzle. CONTROLS: Clicking empty space moves the cursor; clicking a bead swaps it with the cursor. RULE: The blob always centers itself exactly between the cursor and the last moved bead. TRAP: Assuming you could click a bead hidden under the blob, which caused failed inputs.

GOAL: Move two yellow tiles to the top row's specific bracket slots. CONTROLS: Middle arrows rotate the main loop; top arrows rotate only the top row segment. RULE: The top row acts as a separate cycle, allowing tiles to jump between left and right ends without moving the rest. TRAP: Assuming top arrows move all tiles; they only affect the top row, leaving the main loop static.

GOAL: Guide the plug into the green socket. CONTROLS: SPACE rotates, ARROWS move. RULE: Align the plug's prongs with the socket's vertical channel before pushing right. TRAP: Assuming the plug fits without rotating first wastes moves; it must face right.

GOAL: Guide the black shape to the yellow target by navigating around the central mirror. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the black shape directly; the charcoal shape acts as its mirrored reflection. RULE: The mirror reflects horizontal movement, so moving right pushes the reflection left, requiring coordinated positioning. TRAP: Assuming the reflection moves independently wastes time; it always mirrors the black shape's actions.

GOAL: Navigate the checkerboard maze from the start to the green exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character across the grid. RULE: Valid moves connect white cells through open gray corridors; black cells block paths. TRAP: Assuming any adjacent cell is reachable wastes time; only moves through gray connectors work.

GOAL: Move the gray arm so its yellow marker aligns with the fixed yellow notch on the black bar. CONTROLS: Click the blue buttons to shift the arm left or right. RULE: The level ends instantly when the moving yellow marker sits directly above the static one. TRAP: Overthinking complex geometry; the solution was simple horizontal alignment requiring just two clicks.

GOAL: Move the black piece to the target row by aligning it with the mirror's reflection. CONTROLS: Arrows move the currently active object; Space toggles control between the mirror and the piece. RULE: The object with white dots is the one you control; Space swaps which object has the white dots. TRAP: Assuming arrows always move the same object; you must press Space to switch control to the black piece.

GOAL: Flip thirteen specific grid cells to clear the board. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles itself and its orthogonal neighbors. RULE: Clicking a cell twice cancels out, so only parity matters. TRAP: Assuming unconstrained cells could be part of the solution; they must remain untouched.

GOAL: Move the bottom arm to the right to grab the handle. CONTROLS: Pressing buttons shifts one arm left and another right across their shared bar. RULE: An arm can only extend if it has empty space to move into; otherwise, the click fails. TRAP: Believing all buttons move arms the same way wastes time; you must find the specific buttons that retract the blocking middle arm first.

ESTABLISHED: Red bar hinges at dark red center. Clicking top rotates left-to-up. Clicking base rotates up-to-left. Yellow device and green box positions are fixed. FAILED: Assuming red bar only toggles between left and up. Previous attempts to clear level within budget failed using only these two positions. GOAL IS NOT: Simply toggling the red bar between left and up to reach the green box or yellow device. CONTROLS: Clicking red plug top rotates bar counter-clockwise. Clicking red plug base rotates bar clockwise.

GOAL: Move two boxes into the target slots using only two inputs. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the player one grid space; Space grabs or releases a box. RULE: The player pushes boxes by standing behind them, not by pulling. TRAP: Assuming you must walk around to push; instead, stand adjacent and push directly.

GOAL: Match the bottom pink row to the top blue row using the legend. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; Up and Down cycle the symbol under the cursor. RULE: Each column must display the specific partner symbol defined in the top grid. TRAP: Assuming symbols cycle in numeric order wastes time; you must follow the specific legend mapping.

GOAL: Position two shapes so their vertical reflections fill the target outlines above the mirror line. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space cycles selection between the mirror and pieces. RULE: A piece placed below the mirror creates an upside-down reflection above it. TRAP: Forgetting that reflections are vertically flipped, not just mirrored horizontally, leads to incorrect shape orientation.

GOAL: Extend three robotic arms to align with their target markers. CONTROLS: Click buttons to extend arms; buttons remain clickable even when covered. RULE: Arms extend to a fixed hard limit at the frame's edge, not the button position. TRAP: Assuming extended arms block the buttons, which wastes time waiting for them to retract.

GOAL: Reach the exit by moving in large steps across the grid. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player two spaces at a time. RULE: You must land on safe tiles; the enemy occupies specific cells that block your path. TRAP: Assuming you can stop on intermediate tiles between moves or that the enemy moves dynamically.

GOAL: Slide two puzzle pieces into matching outlines to complete two large letter shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space cycles to the next piece or triggers the mirror effect. RULE: Pieces must fit exactly inside their target outlines without overlapping the mirror’s reflection path. TRAP: Moving pieces before selecting the correct one wastes actions and misaligns the final shape.

GOAL: Reorder yellow blocks to match the fixed pink row's sequence. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the selection cursor to cycle through block options. RULE: The static pink row dictated the exact left-to-right order of the answer. TRAP: Assuming the answer followed the legend's order instead of the puzzle's scrambled sequence.

ESTABLISHED: Removing a plus clears the entire vertical wall segment in its column range, not just the plus shape. The plug grid has 1-pixel black separators between pluses. FAILED: Assuming removal only clears the 5x5 plus footprint or trying to clear the level within budget. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing the visible green pluses without managing the black separator lines. CONTROLS: Mouse click removes a plus. Right arrow moves right.

ESTABLISHED: Canvas currently holds white top and purple bottom. Ink tray shows white selected. FAILED: Stamping purple over white produced no visible change or completion. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the displayed picture’s top-to-bottom color order. CONTROLS: Clicking icons changes ink color. Space executes stamp. Arrow keys tilt the stamp angle.

GOAL: Match seven blue glyphs to the bottom yellow row order. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; up/down cycles the glyph at the current slot. RULE: Only rotational orientation matters; mirrored versions count as incorrect. TRAP: Assuming similar-looking shapes are interchangeable, ignoring distinct rotational classes.

GOAL: Drop the plug five cells down to reach the socket. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle colors; click the mouse to run the sequence. RULE: Each column acts as an instruction: two black cells mean move down, white means stop. TRAP: Assuming you need horizontal moves to align the plug; it only moves straight down.

GOAL: Guide the hero to the exit while avoiding lethal traps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the hero one step in that direction. RULE: Entering a trap's cell destroys it, but only if you do not approach from its facing side. TRAP: Assuming all traps can be destroyed by entering them; approaching from the front causes instant failure.

GOAL: Align seven glyph slots to match target shapes defined by size classes. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; up and down inputs rotate the current slot’s glyph through its cycle. RULE: Match shapes by distinct class signatures, not just pixel size, as same-sized targets may differ. TRAP: Assuming all 10-pixel targets are identical wastes moves; they belong to different shape classes.

GOAL: Guide the purple square to the glowing blob at the end of the dotted path. CONTROLS: Click within the purple square’s ring to move it one hop in that direction. RULE: Each hop moves the piece exactly eight units in the clicked direction. TRAP: Assuming you can land directly on the blob from far away; you must stop adjacent to it first.

GOAL: Reach the pink marker by climbing to the upper chamber. CONTROLS: Click green tiles to clear paths; use arrow keys to move. RULE: You must clear the specific tile above your target to open the vertical shaft. TRAP: Assuming all green tiles are necessary; clicking extra tiles wastes moves and delays the climb.

GOAL: Fill the four empty slots to match the color sequence shown at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a colored button at the bottom to select it, then click an empty slot to place the color. RULE: Each color can only be used once; placing a color removes its button from the bottom row. TRAP: Assuming the bottom row order matters, when only the top sequence defines the correct arrangement.

GOAL: Match eight rotating dial symbols to the specific bar patterns shown on the side. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between tiles; UP and DOWN rotate the selected dial’s symbol. RULE: Each tile holds two linked glyphs that turn together; align both to the target shape. TRAP: Assuming symbols cycle independently per tile wastes time; all tiles of the same type share one fixed rotation sequence.

GOAL: Merge small parts into a large yellow piece and move it to touch the target blob. CONTROLS: Clicking empty space drags a piece there; clicking between two close pieces merges them instantly. RULE: Pieces merge automatically if they end up within six units of each other after any move. TRAP: Thinking you must move pieces to exact centers; merging happens automatically if they are close enough.

GOAL: Slide the platform to position a splitting block over two side notches. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the platform; space drops the block. RULE: The block duplicates, with halves sliding off opposite ends to fill gaps. TRAP: Assuming the block stays centered on the platform rather than splitting and sliding off.

GOAL: Align two crosses so their arms cover all matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected cross three spaces; Space switches selection. RULE: Move only in multiples of three to hit exact center coordinates. TRAP: Assuming dots are collected on contact; they are not, precise alignment is required.

GOAL: Extend green and yellow bars so their tips align perfectly with the target plus sign. CONTROLS: Clicking each color’s arrow adds length to that specific bar. RULE: Each click extends the bar by exactly three units, so count carefully to land on the center. TRAP: Thinking the bar head stops at the tip; the dot is the actual endpoint, so overshooting the visible edge misses the target.

GOAL: Position three shapes to cover all target dots using their specific coverage patterns. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space cycles to the next shape in the rotation order. RULE: Shapes cover dots only when their center aligns with the grid's valid spacing for that shape. TRAP: Assuming any valid geometric center works; you must also ensure the center is reachable via whole-step moves from the start.

GOAL: Map colored blocks to seven target slots to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click a color button, then click an empty slot to place it. Press Space to test the sequence. RULE: The pipe diverts the reading order, inserting the green column between the second and fourth red slots. TRAP: Assuming left-to-right order ignores the pipe, causing the final block to fail its position check.

GOAL: Place the white diamond onto the purple ring marker. CONTROLS: Click the white diamond to move it; click the gray diamond to swap their positions. RULE: The white diamond always sits exactly opposite the gray diamond across the central square. TRAP: Thinking the ring disappears when touched; it stays until the white diamond is correctly positioned on it.

GOAL: Place seven letters across three linked boxes in strict reading order. CONTROLS: Press letter keys to select, click slots to place, and hit space to submit. RULE: Portals redirect the sequence into connected boxes, resuming on the next available slot. TRAP: Assuming red slots are filled consecutively ignores how portals interrupt the linear path.

GOAL: Route the signal by placing a diverter to read the nested green box. CONTROLS: Click the diverter button, then a red slot to insert the green sequence. RULE: The diverter slot determines exactly where the green box’s items appear in the final chain. TRAP: Assuming the green box’s pre-placed item was static; it only matters if you route through it.

GOAL: Touch the floating block to mark all three targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the beam head and retract or extend the light. RULE: The beam only hits blocks aligned with its current row and length. TRAP: Assuming vertical moves drag distant blocks; they only move when the beam pushes them.

GOAL: Cover every dot using three movable shapes: a bar, an X, and a diamond. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape; spacebar switches to the next shape. RULE: Shapes cover dots only when centered precisely so their geometry aligns with the dot grid. TRAP: Assuming you can cycle shapes freely; you must plan moves in the fixed bar-X-diamond order.

GOAL: Place two connectors on adjacent red slots so the blue box’s three-letter block repeats identically when traversed twice. CONTROLS: Click connector buttons to place portals on red slots, click letter tiles to assign them to empty slots, and press Space to verify the solution. RULE: The blue box’s content must form a repeating three-letter pattern that matches the required target sequence exactly during both passes. TRAP: Assuming connectors can be placed anywhere fails; they must be adjacent to force the specific double traversal needed for the repeating block.

GOAL: Merge scattered pairs into single items, then combine those into one final result. CONTROLS: Clicking near two close items merges them into one. RULE: Only items within a short distance merge; click exactly between them. TRAP: Clicking too far away does nothing, wasting a move, so check the gap size first.

GOAL: Fill three colored boxes with matching item pairs using three connector slots. CONTROLS: Click source items to select them, then click empty slots to place them. Press Space to submit. RULE: Each connector links to a specific color box, dictating which items go there based on the first pre-filled symbol. TRAP: Assuming connectors are interchangeable; they are fixed paths, so placing a wrong connector breaks the entire chain logic.

GOAL: Slide the knob left to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob along the rail. RULE: Aligning the lit cells with the panel diamond pushes the knob further left. TRAP: You might think you need to solve a complex pattern to win, but simple alignment is all that matters.

GOAL: Route the path through nested boxes by placing connectors to bridge gaps between red, blue, and green slots. CONTROLS: Click outline buttons to place connectors, solid buttons to fill slots, and space to test the path. RULE: Connectors must align with the pre-filled yellow marker to establish a continuous traversal order across all segments. TRAP: Assuming you can fill empty slots without first establishing a valid connector bridge leads to immediate failure.

GOAL: Move the plunger knob up into the handle. CONTROLS: Click white grid cells to shrink the knob; press UP to move it. RULE: The knob must shrink to two units wide to pass the charcoal neck. TRAP: Trying to push the full-sized knob through the narrow gap wastes time.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so all colored dots align with their target positions on the track. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to rotate clockwise, or the green arrow to rotate counter-clockwise. RULE: Each click shifts the entire ring by one position; only relative order matters, not absolute angle. TRAP: Trying to move individual dots. They are locked to the ring; you must rotate the whole assembly.

ESTABLISHED: The two blue squares successfully merged into a single block, but the level remains active. The black arch structure remains intact, with yellow and orange regions still touching along their seam. FAILED: Merging the squares alone did not clear the level. Pressing SPACE after the merge produced no visible result. Moving the merged block via left/right inputs did not trigger completion. GOAL IS NOT: Simply merging the two blue squares. Separating the yellow and orange regions is impossible with current tools. Placing the block in the bottom socket is unreachable. CONTROLS: Arrow ke

GOAL: Align the knob, then fire a beam to shatter the red seals blocking the path to the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; clicking matched cells fires a beam in the direction of the knob’s blue side. RULE: The beam travels along tubes and destroys objects containing the letter "r" upon impact. TRAP: Assuming the beam pushes caps; it actually destroys red-sealed obstacles, clearing the way instead.

GOAL: Slide the block onto the marked cross to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block in cardinal directions. RULE: The block slides until it hits a wall or obstacle. TRAP: Assuming the block stops immediately after one press; it travels the full path.
